name: Ebigane
body:
EBIGANE
CR 6

This hulking buffalo-like predator has leathery batwings, red glowing eyes, and elongated canines that glisten with the promise of blood.

XP 2,400
NE Large magical beast
Init +4; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision; Perception +16

DEFENSE

AC 19, touch 9, flat-footed 19 (+10 natural, –1 size)
hp 76 (9d10+27)
Fort +9, Ref +6, Will +5

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft., fly 70 ft. (average)
Melee bite +12 (2d6+4 plus grab and poison), 2 claws +12 (1d6+4)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 5 ft.
Special Attacks blood drain (1d2 Con), consuming siphon, creeping paralysis, grab, hemovoric drinker, poison

STATISTICS

Str 18, Dex 10, Con 17, Int 6, Wis 15, Cha 11
Base Atk +9; CMB +14 (+18 grapple); CMD 24 (28 vs. trip)
Feats Cunning, Hover, Improved Initiative, Skill Focus (Perception), Wingover
Skills Fly +9, Perception +16
Languages Common

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Consuming Siphon (Ex)

Against helpless or paralyzed targets, an ebigane’s blood drain doubles to 2d2 Constitution damage.

Creeping Paralysis (Ex)

A creature who fails three consecutive saves against an ebigane’s poison is paralyzed for 24 hours.

Hemovoric Drinker (Su)

When an ebigane deals Constitution damage with blood drain, it heals 1d6 hit points per point of Constitution damage dealt. However, it gains no healing from points of Constitution damage which exceed the victim’s current Constitution score.

Poison (Ex)

Bite—injury; save Fort DC 17; frequency 1/round for 6 rounds; effect paralyzed for 1 round; cure 1 save.

ECOLOGY

Environment temperate mountains
Organization solitary
Treasure incidental

Ebigane are vampiric monstrosities that arise from the magical machinations of evil spellcasters. They resemble of a hybrid of a buffalo and a vampire bat, possessing a large, bulllike torso, massive batwings, glowing red eyes, and enlarged canines. Ebigane make their lairs in mountain roosts, from which they hunt in a massive radius for humanoids and large beasts, before returning with the still-living carcasses of their prey. They have the dimensions of a water buffalo, but with batlike wings.

The saliva of an ebigane contains a paralytic agent, allowing it to immobilize its prey and carry them off to its lair. The ebigane then slowly drains the blood of the creature. This experience is incredibly painful, for the saliva is in no way anesthetic. Periodically, the ebigane gives its prey time to replenish their blood supply while it goes off to hunt. It’s common for the ebigane to have far more prey in its lair than it needs and to slowly feed various creature for months, taking just a bit from each one. Occasionally, it will tire of some or all of its prey, picking them up and dropping their paralyzed bodies off the side of the mountain, where they fall to their deaths, feeling each painful jolt as they cascade down the mountain’s surface, unable to do anything to save themselves.

Ebigane live to torture and feed off their prey. They have no desire to procreate and will attempt to kill or drive off other ebigane on sight. Their sense of self-preservation comes from the fact that dying would prevent them from feeding, not from any great love of life.
